ci_sentinels.note: Both fields are CI-resolved sentinels. An evidence commit cannot name its own SHA before it exists, and the PR head moves with every push, so hand-authored values here would be stale the moment they were written. The proof-binding validator resolves both from the checkout it is running in.

known_limitations: The runner has never executed end to end against staging. workflow_dispatch workflows are only dispatchable once they are on the default branch, so staging-proof-runner.yml cannot be triggered from this PR. Proven here: the admission boundary and the workflow's declared isolation. Not proven: a successful spawn, a real receipt, or the exit-status pass-through.

The first dispatch after merge is the real acceptance test. canonical-reference-bootstrap-report (writes:false) is the right first dispatch — it exercises environment binding, staging assertion, spawn, receipt and artifact upload without writing anything.

The workflow-shape assertions read the YAML as text. They confirm what the file says; they do not confirm the Actions runtime honours it. That property is evidenced by staging-db-proof.yml behaving this way in production CI, not by anything this PR measures.

The ancestry gate binds the registry to reviewed code, not the reviewer to good judgement. It guarantees the staging-proof-commands.ts that admits a key reached main through the normal PR path. It does nothing about a command admitted INTO main by a review that should have refused it, and nothing about someone who can write to main directly.

writes:true is a declaration, not an enforcement. The registry records whether a command writes so a reviewer can see it; nothing here stops a command declared writes:false from writing. The containment that actually holds is the credential boundary — the job releases only project-scoped staging keys, and a Supabase API key is a project-scoped JWT.

No live-DB proof is claimed for this lane's own code, because none of it touches the database. The staging receipt cited under hosted_verification is the run-level receipt ci.yml produces for every PR at this head; it is evidence that the branch does not break the staging path, not evidence about the runner.

receipt.receipt_github_sha_note: The receipt records GITHUB_SHA, which for a pull_request event is the synthetic merge ref GitHub builds from the PR head and the base — not the PR head itself. GitHub reports it as this PR's merge_commit_sha, and the PR head at that run was 2d34269ff. Both are recorded rather than collapsing them, because a bundle that claimed the receipt names the head would be false.

runtime_proof.significance: The suites in this chain are `{ skip: skipReason }`-gated on SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, so a missing credential produces a passing job with every test skipped. `skipped: 0` — corroborated by 17-21s per test against a total of 115.8s — is what establishes the suite actually executed against staging rather than short-circuiting.
runtime_proof.what_this_is_and_is_not: This is the run-level staging receipt for the required `Writable DB proof (staging only)` job at this lane's anchor. It is NOT evidence about the runner this PR adds. The runner is a workflow_dispatch entry point that has never been dispatched — it cannot be, because workflow_dispatch reads the workflow definition from the default branch and this workflow is not on main yet, and because the runner refuses any ref not reachable from the default branch. The controls this PR actually adds are proven by the seven mutations in mutation_proof, not by this receipt. The receipt is recorded because the lane_type is `runtime`, which forces the `app-runtime` proof profile, and because it is honest evidence that the anchor passes the live-DB gate — not because it exercises the new code.
